risks.risk: Exact model mismatch (could be another Yamaha 61-key model), which affects value.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear close-up photo of the model label/serial sticker (usually on the back or underside) and the full front panel including the display area.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic Yamaha 61-key portable keyboard (worst case vs PSR-E453).

risks.risk: Some keys/buttons may be faulty (dead keys, stuck keys) or have intermittent issues not visible in a still photo.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video: power on + play a scale across the full keyboard + press all buttons/controls once (with the screen showing activity).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully guaranteed working (worst case).

risks.risk: No crackle/noise claim may be false; speaker/headphone output could have noise or distortion.
risks.proof: Ask for a clip recording audio through the built-in speakers and/or headphone output while playing a few notes and changing volume.
risks.if_unproven: Price as having unknown audio condition (worst case).

risks.risk: Adapter may be missing or not the correct specification.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the adapter (label/spec) next to the keyboard and a quick power-on demonstration.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the model/serial label (back/underside) showing 'PSR-E453' if that’s what it is.
Video proof: power on, screen on, play all keys (left to right) and press key buttons/controls.
Audio test clip: play notes through speakers and show volume changes (and headphone output if available).
Photo of the adapter with its label/spec + quick power-on.
response.reason: Photo 0 confirms it’s a Yamaha 61-key keyboard, but the exact PSR-E453 model and the working/adapter claims cannot be verified from the single image. Without proof, the correct worst-case pricing is uncertain.
